verses.text: King Belshazzar gave a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine with them.

While Belshazzar was drinking his wine, he ordered that the gold and silver cups be brought in. His father Nebuchadnezzar had taken them from the temple in Jerusalem. The king wanted to drink from them with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
So they brought in the gold cups that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem. The king and his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
As they drank the wine, they praised their gods made of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and began writing on the plaster wall of the king's palace, near the lampstand. The king watched the hand as it wrote.
The king's face turned pale, and he was so terrified that his legs gave way and his knees knocked together.

The king shouted for the enchanters, astrologers, and fortune-tellers to be brought in. He said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me what it means will be dressed in purple and have a gold chain put around his neck. He will become the third highest ruler in the kingdom."
Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
So King Belshazzar became even more terrified, and his face grew even paler. His nobles were confused.
When the queen mother heard the voices of the king and his nobles, she came into the banquet hall. She said, "May the king live forever! Do not be alarmed or look so pale.

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In your father's time, he was found to have insight, understanding, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and fortune-tellers.

This man Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, has an excellent mind, with knowledge and understanding. He can explain dreams, solve riddles, and work out difficult problems. Call for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means."
So Daniel was brought before the king. The king said to him, "Are you Daniel, one of the captives my father the king brought from Judah?
I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you and that you have insight, understanding, and great wisdom.
The wise men and enchanters were brought to me to read this writing and tell me what it means, but they could not explain it.

But I have heard that you can explain things and solve difficult problems. If you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will be dressed in purple and have a gold chain put around your neck. You will become the third highest ruler in the kingdom."
Daniel answered the king, "Keep your gifts for yourself, and give your rewards to someone else. But I will read the writing for the king and tell him what it means.
"Your Majesty, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.

Because of the greatness God gave him, people of every nation and language trembled with fear before him. He put to death anyone he wanted to kill and spared anyone he wanted to spare. He raised up anyone he wanted to raise up and brought down anyone he wanted to bring down.
But when his heart became proud and stubborn, he was removed from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.

He was driven away from people, and he was given the mind of an animal. He lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like cattle. His body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until he admitted that the Most High God rules over human kingdoms and sets over them anyone he wishes.
"But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not humbled yourself, even though you knew all this.

Instead, you have set yourself up against the Lord of heaven. You had the cups from his temple brought to you, and you and your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods made of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, gods that cannot see or hear or understand. But you did not honor the God who holds your life in his hand and controls everything you do.
That is why he sent the hand that wrote this message.
"This is what was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
"This is what these words mean: MENE means God has counted the days of your rule and brought it to an end.
TEKEL means you have been weighed on the scales and found not good enough.
PERES means your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
Then at Belshazzar's command, Daniel was dressed in purple, a gold chain was put around his neck, and it was announced that he was the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, king of the Babylonians, was killed.
And Darius the Mede took over the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.
